fields.notes: Wishbone B4 security is limited to signaling primitives (LOCK + RMW + user-defined TGA/TGC tags + ERR_O / RTY_O termination) - not cryptographic primitives. End-to-end confidentiality and integrity must be provided by upper layers (dedicated crypto IP, secure boot ROM, address-space controllers). Wishbone's clear-text bus signaling is appropriate for on-chip use; off-chip extensions over public boards may require integrator-added bus-encryption wrappers.

wishbone_security_features.name: [LOCK_O] / [LOCK_I] locked bus cycle
wishbone_security_features.purpose: Uninterruptible bus cycle for indivisible semaphore operations.

wishbone_security_features.name: [TGA_O()] address tag
wishbone_security_features.purpose: User-defined; may carry 'protected memory' or memory-management semantics.

wishbone_security_features.name: [TGC_O()] cycle tag
wishbone_security_features.purpose: User-defined; may mark interrupt-ack / cache-control / restricted-access cycles.

wishbone_security_features.name: [ERR_O] / [ERR_I] abnormal termination
wishbone_security_features.purpose: Allows SLAVE to reject an access (e.g. protected region).

what_is_NOT_in_the_spec: No confidentiality / encryption at the bus layer.
No formal secure/non-secure transfer signal (unlike AHB5 HNONSEC / AXI AxPROT[1]).
No formal privileged/user transfer signal (unlike AHB HPROT[1] / APB PPROT[0]).
secure_integration_responsibilities: Address-space partitioning via INTERCON-level access-control filters.
Watchdog timeouts: INTERCON SHOULD include a watchdog (RECOMMENDATION 3.10).
Optional ERR_O / RTY_O termination by SLAVE-side access-control filter.

extraction_hints: Look for key-management, side-channel, secure-boot sections.
